title: Keyboard Manager Shortcut doesn't work upon opening new programs.

judgment.rationale: The report identifies a Keyboard Manager regression, but it still lacks the exact saved mapping and a fresh diagnostic bundle that would separate an App/Menu key translation problem from an app-specific focus or privilege boundary issue.
evidence: The report says a physical App/Menu key is remapped to Left Win and stops behaving as remapped when newly opened programs receive focus.
The issue already includes the module, PowerToys version 0.100.2, Windows build 26200, and the fact that PowerToys is running non-elevated.
No screenshot of the saved remap, no narrowed repro across specific app types, and no bug report ZIP are attached.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for the exact remap entry, a narrowed current-build repro, and a fresh /bugreport capture before choosing a Keyboard Manager fix path.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys code change may be relevant, but the current public evidence is still too incomplete to pick a specific Keyboard Manager path safely.

issue_context.summary: The reporter says a Keyboard Manager remap from the keyboard App/Menu key to Left Win stopped working correctly in newly opened programs after an update, even though the same key should open Start consistently.
known_information: The report is filed against PowerToys 0.100.2 on Windows 11 build 26200 from a per-user Microsoft Store install.
The configured scenario uses a physical App/Menu key on the right side of the keyboard and expects it to behave like Left Win.
The failure is described as focus-sensitive: after opening a new program, the key behaves like its default App/Menu action instead of the configured remap.
The issue is labeled Issue-Bug, Needs-Triage, and Product-Keyboard Manager.
inferences: The regression may depend on how Keyboard Manager distinguishes the App/Menu virtual key from Windows-key modifiers after focus switches into certain app types.
The current report does not yet show whether the problem is global, elevation-specific, or limited to a subset of windows such as elevated, UWP, or freshly launched apps.
issue_context.analysis: The module and symptom are clear enough to avoid a generic “send more logs” response, but they are not yet specific enough to isolate whether the bug sits in source-key detection, remap persistence, or app-bound input handling. The next useful step is to capture the exact mapping and a fresh reproduction trace rather than guessing at a code change.
initial_investigation: A focused repository scan found generic modifier-release and scan-code handling in src/modules/KeyboardManager/common/Helpers.cpp, which is plausible background for App/Menu remaps but does not by itself identify this exact regression.
No linked fix, maintainer reply, or duplicate marker is currently present on the upstream issue.

information_gaps.information: A screenshot of the exact Keyboard Manager remap entry for the App/Menu key.
information_gaps.why_needed: This confirms whether the issue is a single-key remap, a shortcut mapping, or a different configuration than the body text implies.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Open Keyboard Manager, show the saved remap row for this key, and upload a screenshot through the GitHub web UI.

information_gaps.information: A short numbered repro that names one or two specific apps where the remap immediately falls back to the default App/Menu behavior, including whether those apps are elevated.
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes a global remap regression from an app-type or privilege-boundary problem.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: List the exact steps from a fresh PowerToys launch, then name the affected apps and whether PowerToys or those apps are running elevated.

information_gaps.information: A fresh PowerToys diagnostic ZIP captured immediately after reproducing the fallback-to-default behavior.
information_gaps.why_needed: The packaged logs are the fastest public-safe way to confirm that Keyboard Manager loaded the remap and to inspect any hook or config errors around the failing key.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce the problem and then submit a new comment containing /bugreport immediately afterward.

actions.label: Request App/Menu remap evidence

comment.body:
Thanks for the clear module, version, and key details. To narrow this to the right Keyboard Manager path, please provide:

1. A screenshot of the exact App/Menu remap entry in Keyboard Manager.
2. Short numbered steps from a fresh PowerToys launch that name one or two apps where the key falls back to its default App/Menu behavior, and whether those apps are elevated.
3. A fresh diagnostic ZIP by reproducing the issue and then posting a comment with /bugreport immediately afterward.

That will distinguish a general App/Menu remap regression from an app-specific focus or privilege-boundary issue.
